prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows an indoor room with a ceiling and a window wall 3 to 5 metres behind the foreground, where a man in a plaid shirt stands roughly 0.6 to 1.0 metre in front of the camera wearer while holding a dark garment on a hanger even closer at 0.3 to 0.5 metres (within arm's reach of both the man and the camera wearer). In frame 1, a second person stands about 2.5 to 3 metres away to the right and behind the foreground man (roughly 2 metres behind him), partially occluded by the held garment, and reappears as a dim silhouette at the bottom-right edge in frame 4. Across frames 1 to 3, the held hanger and dark garment become intensely bright white as the man brings them closer to the camera wearer's right side (to within 0.3 metres), temporarily occluding his own chin and chest before lowering them in frames 4 and 5 as the camera wearer's own left hand enters the lower-left foreground at about 0.3 to 0.4 metres to touch his right shoulder. From the silhouette profiles and glasses geometry in the depth map, the foreground man faces slightly downward and to the right in frames 1 to 3 before turning to face directly toward the camera wearer while tilting his head down in frames 4 and 5, with his lower torso remaining out of view below the bottom frame edge throughout. The depth map makes it much easier than RGB alone to separate the black garment and hanger from the man's dark inner shirt and to gauge the exact proximity jump in frames 2 and 3, though it looks unreliable where the nearest garment region saturates to flat white and where distant exterior trees through the window are flattened into the same dark depth plane as the interior wall.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates the foreground silhouettes against an unlabelled black background, showing the main man in front of the camera wearer (at roughly 0.6 to 1.0 metre) on the left in frame 1 and centered in frames 2 to 5, along with a second person on the right in frame 1 and bottom-right in frames 4 and 5 at about 2.5 to 3 metres distance. In frame 1, the map separates the main man (lime green) from the dark garment he holds within arm's reach in front of his chest (brown) and the distant person (pink) to his right, while also falsely labelling an outdoor red patio umbrella visible through the window 4 to 5 metres behind them as an 'umbrella' just above the garment. In frames 2 and 3, as the garment and hanger approach the camera wearer and occlude the man's neck and lower face, the segmentation merges the man, the hanger, and the garment into a single pink 'person' mask, while picking up a small distant 'person' mask (mannequin/clothing rack at 3 to 4 metres on the left) in frames 3 and 5. In frames 4 and 5, as the man faces the camera wearer with his head tilted down and his lower body cropped out below the frame, the camera wearer's own left arm enters from the bottom-left within 0.4 metres (segmented as a separate lime-green region in frame 5) and reaches the man's right shoulder. While segmentation clearly delineates the boundary between the camera wearer's reaching arm and the man's torso in frame 5 and spots the small background person on the bottom right of frame 4 that blends into the dark RGB edge, it is unreliable in merging the held clothing into the 'person' mask in frames 2–5, omitting all room structure, and hallucinating multiple overlapping 'person' labels on the background mannequin and the wearer's arm in frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders sparse 2D facial keypoints and shoulder/arm skeletal lines for the foreground man standing 0.6 to 1.0 metre in front of the camera wearer on a completely black background, omitting all background walls, the distant second person (2.5 to 3 metres away), and the held garment and hanger. In frame 1, yellow facial dots show the man facing slightly to the right and downward while his right shoulder, elbow, and detailed magenta right-hand finger skeleton (within arm's reach at roughly 0.5 metres on the left) and his left arm (extending right) hold up the unseen garment, with his torso below the chest out of view. In frames 2 and 3, as the garment and hanger move closer and occlude his body and lower face, the pose map collapses into compact clusters of yellow facial dots and short neck/upper-chest segments turned to the right, losing both hands entirely. By frames 4 and 5, the symmetrical arrangement of yellow eye, nose, and mouth keypoints shows the man facing straight toward the camera wearer with his head angled down above a horizontal yellow shoulder line, while in frame 5 a magenta hand skeleton appears on the lower left at 0.4 metres where the camera wearer's left hand reaches onto the man's right shoulder. The pose map makes the man's head rotation from right-angled to frontal and the exact finger articulation of the hands in frames 1 and 5 much clearer than the motion-blurred RGB alone, but it is highly unreliable in frames 2 and 3 due to heavy occlusion from the black garment and in frame 5 where it mistakenly attaches the camera wearer's reaching left hand to the foreground man's right wrist/shoulder joint.
